label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
**4 out of 5 stars.** We would buy the PT-20 again, but it was a significant purchase for our congregation, and I think a church under 100 members might do just fine with a less expensive camera.

We bought ours from Chancel AV in February 2026 for $2,140, plus $95 for the wall mount. It replaced the webcam we had used to livestream worship since 2020. We have the camera mounted on the balcony rail at the back of our nave, which is 92 feet long. It runs into OBS on our old office PC, and we stream to our YouTube channel, where we usually have 30 to 60 viewers on a Sunday.

The 20x optical zoom has been useful at that distance. We have nine presets stored: altar, pulpit, lectern, font, choir loft, piano, a wide view, and two for the chancel steps. Erik, our 16-year-old acolyte, operates it from the free web app on a tablet. He learned his way around it in an afternoon.

We did have a problem at first. On the first Sunday, the presets had drifted a few degrees by the time we got to the sermon. A firmware update to version 2.4 in March fixed that for us. The manual is thin and badly translated, so I would not count on it to answer every setup question. Marcy at Chancel AV was excellent on the phone when we needed help.

The camera offers 1080p at 60 frames per second, NDI HX and a regular HDMI output. It also uses PoE, which meant one cable up to the balcony. I’m not an engineer, but that made for a simpler installation than I had expected.

The picture is a substantial improvement over the webcam. Delores, who is 82 and homebound, called to tell me she could finally read the hymn numbers on the board. That meant more to me than any list of specifications.

It has its limits, though. At the Easter Vigil in April, we sang the first “Christ the Lord Is Risen Today” with only candles for light. The picture got grainy, but it stayed usable. Our old webcam would have shown little more than dots. The autofocus also hunts when someone walks between the camera and the pulpit, so we lock the focus on our presets.

One other thing worth saying: **this camera did nothing to fix our sound problem.** Audio is not the camera’s job, and a church with trouble being heard should not expect a new camera to solve it.

For us, the better view from the back of the nave and the ability to move between parts of the service have made it worthwhile. I’m glad we bought it, but I would encourage another small parish to look at its room, its budget and its sound setup before spending this much.
